items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I remember hearing a saxophone player at the time, Ross Gorman, and he had an orchestra and he played at a club, I believe it was called the Monte Carlo Club.

ctx.x: Can you remember any particular music you heard on the family phonograph that impressed you at an early age?

Well, at that particular age, if we're going to go back as far as that, seven or eight years old, that would be pretty hard to say. I used to hear broadcasts from the nightclubs, and of course they were -- the quality was ridiculous. But I remember hearing a saxophone player at the time, Ross Gorman, and he had an orchestra and he played at a club, I believe it was called the Monte Carlo Club. That was

back in the '20s, then I used to hear Charley Johnson's Orchestra, from Small's Paradise. Which also I was very impressed with. But they used to come on rather late, and I had to kind of sneak, you know, listening to them, because I was supposed to be in bed and asleep.
